title: Joyce:
title_q: She Didn't Have to Sell the Cow
title_short: Vishal · Joyce: She Didn't Have to Sell the Cow
headline: Joyce's problem was timing, not income. For her first daughter's school fees she sold a cow. For the second, she took a Kiva loan and kept it.
story: Vishal learns the most when he meets borrowers in person. In Nairobi he met Joyce, who had taken a Kiva loan for her daughter's school fees.

There, school fees are paid as one lump sum at the start of the year. For her first daughter, Joyce sold her cow. For her second, she took a Kiva loan, paid the fees, kept the cow and paid the loan back from her farm income.
The whole second take, in order, so the viewer hears where he met her and how the loan came in. It ends on the title beat: she was able to pay fees and not sell her cow.
do: Cold open on the cow line with the hook text, then jump back to the start of the take.
Keep the take whole and in order: opener, Nairobi and Joyce, the lump sum, daughter 1, daughter 2, paid back.
Keep the context line “I remember in Nairobi … I spoke to Joyce who had taken a loan from Kiva” in full.
Name super after the hook: “Vishal Ghotge” / “CEO at Kiva”, small, lower left.
End on the title beat from P1000920: “it was great to see that she was able to pay fees and not sell her cow.”
dont: Never drop his words inside a line. Cut only stutters and pauses.
No name super for Joyce: she is not on camera.
No name plate, logo or fade at 0:00.
Never “investment” on screen. Never the transcript's spelling of his name.
No big lime captions. Brit's caption spec only.

transcript:
--- P1000921.MOV ---
[00:06.5] You know one of the reasons I really like visiting our entrepreneurs and hearing their stories in person is because you learn so much.
[00:19.2] I remember in Nairobi I visited a bunch of our entrepreneurs and I spoke to Joyce who had taken a loan from Kiva for her daughter's school fees
[00:31.3] and I always wondered how can Joyce pay that back, how is it going to work
[00:36.9] and I learned from her that it's not that she had an income coming through the year for her, it's that she didn't have money to pay her school fees lump sum at the beginning of the year and that's how it works in Nairobi that you have to pay the money up front
[00:55.0] and for her first daughter she ended up selling her cow so she could get school fees and pay
[01:02.1] but for her second daughter she decided to take a Kiva loan, she was able to take that loan, pay school fees and not have to sell her cow
[01:12.3] and she was able to pay it off because she had her agriculture business that gave her monthly income.
[01:19.1] So it's just fascinating how things work and what limitations people have and how they use Kiva loans to be able to work with their life circumstances.
[01:36.3] Yeah, you learn so much when you talk to our borrowers and entrepreneurs.
--- P1000920.MOV ---
[00:00.9] Okay. [do not use: crew talk]
[00:01.8] See, the reason I find it so valuable to meet our entrepreneurs in person is you learn so much when you actually see and talk to them and understand the situations they're going through.
[00:14.9] I remember when I was in Nairobi talking to Joyce.
[00:17.8] I learned so much about education loans and how people think about it.
[00:22.8] So I always wondered how do people take loans for school fees and how do they pay them off?
[00:30.4] How does that work?
[00:31.9] And when I was in Nairobi, I completely understood this.
[00:34.6] So Joyce was trying to put her girls through school and the way the system works is you have to pay the fees for school right up front, you know, the entire year's school fees.
[00:48.9] And Joyce just did not have the money to be able to do that.
[00:54.1] And for her first daughter, she actually, she had cows and she sold one of her cows so that she could, you know, she could pay the fees.
[01:05.3] Second time around, for her second daughter, she took a loan from Kiva
[01:09.5] and what that helped her with is it's not that she didn't have cash flow, there was a lot of money coming in through her agricultural activities, but she just didn't have working capital to pay for school fees.
[01:22.8] So the Kiva loan allowed her to pay the school fees and not sell her cow and she was able to pay it back in installments because she had money coming in.
[01:33.1] And so it's just fascinating when you see how people's lives work, what this loan can mean for them and how it supports people in very different ways.
[01:43.2] And so
[01:43.6] It was great to see that she was able to pay fees and not sell her cow.
[01:48.6] So I just thought I'd share that.
[01:51.5] Awesome. [do not use: crew talk]
